sanskrit: devānām api maudgalya kāṅkṣitā sā gatiḥ parā duṣprāpā paramā siddhir agamyā kāmagocaraiḥ
english: O Maudgalya, even the gods desire that supreme goal; the highest perfection is hard to attain and lies beyond the reach of those governed by desires.

sanskrit: trayastriṃśad ime lokāḥ śeṣā lokā manīṣibhiḥ gamyante niyamaiḥ śreṣṭhair dānair vā vidhipūrvakaiḥ
english: These thirty-three worlds — the remaining worlds are reached by the wise through excellent disciplines or through gifts given according to proper rite.

sanskrit: seyaṃ dānakṛtā vyuṣṭir atra prāptā sukhāvahā tāṃ bhuṅkṣva sukṛtair labdhāṃ tapasā dyotitaprabhaḥ
english: This prosperity, earned by your gift, has been attained here and brings joy; enjoy it, O one whose radiance is kindled by austerity — it was won by meritorious deeds.

sanskrit: etat svargasukhaṃ vipra lokā nānāvidhās tathā guṇāḥ svargasya proktās te doṣān api nibodha me
english: Such is the bliss of heaven, O brahmin; such are the many kinds of worlds, and the virtues of heaven have been told to you — now hear from me its faults as well.

sanskrit: kṛtasya karmaṇas tatra bhujyate yat phalaṃ divi na cānyat kriyate karma mūlacchedena bhujyate
english: There in heaven the fruit of deeds already done is enjoyed; no new karma is created — one consumes entirely, down to the root.

sanskrit: so 'tra doṣo mama matas tasyānte patanaṃ ca yat sukhavyāptamanaskānāṃ patanaṃ yac ca mudgala
english: This I regard as a fault in it: the fall at its end, O Mudgala — and the fall of those whose minds are wholly absorbed in pleasure.

sanskrit: asaṃtoṣaḥ parītāpo dṛṣṭvā dīptatarāḥ śriyaḥ yad bhavaty avare sthāne sthitānāṃ tac ca duṣkaram
english: Discontent and anguish arise in those stationed at a lower place when they behold the more resplendent glories — that too is hard to bear.

sanskrit: saṃjñāmohaś ca patatāṃ rajasā ca pradharṣaṇam pramlāneṣu ca mālyeṣu tataḥ pipatiṣor bhayam
english: There is confusion of mind in those who fall, the assault of rajas, and when the garlands begin to wilt, the dread of impending descent.

sanskrit: ā brahmabhavanād ete doṣā maudgalya dāruṇāḥ nākaloke sukṛtināṃ guṇās tv ayutaśo nṛṇām
english: These terrible flaws extend even to the abode of Brahmā, O Maudgalya; yet in the imperishable world the virtues of the meritorious are ten-thousandfold for men.

sanskrit: ayaṃ tv anyo guṇaḥ śreṣṭhaś cyutānāṃ svargato mune śubhānuśayayogena manuṣyeṣūpajāyate
english: This, however, is another surpassing virtue for those who fall from heaven, O sage: through the connection of auspicious residual merit they are reborn among humans.

sanskrit: tatrāpi sumahābhāgaḥ sukhabhāg abhijāyate na cet saṃbudhyate tatra gacchaty adhamatāṃ tataḥ
english: There too one is born greatly fortunate and partakes of happiness; but if one does not attain awakening there, one descends further to a lower state.

sanskrit: iha yat kriyate karma tat paratropabhujyate karmabhūmir iyaṃ brahman phalabhūmir asau matā
english: Whatever karma is performed here is enjoyed in the beyond; this world is held to be the field of action, O brahmin, and that world is held to be the field of fruit.

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ yan māṃ pṛcchasi mudgala tavānukampayā sādho sādhu gacchāma māciram
english: All this that you asked me, O Mudgala, has been told to you out of compassion; now, O virtuous one, let us go — delay no longer.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca etac chrutvā tu maudgalyo vākyaṃ vimamṛśe dhiyā vimṛśya ca muniśreṣṭho devadūtam uvāca ha
english: Vyāsa said: Having heard these words, Maudgalya reflected with his mind; and having reflected, that foremost of sages thus addressed the divine messenger.

sanskrit: devadūta namas te 'stu gaccha tāta yathāsukham mahādoṣeṇa me kāryaṃ na svargeṇa sukhena vā
english: O divine messenger, homage to you — go, dear one, as you please; I have no business with something so greatly flawed, nor with heaven or its pleasures.

sanskrit: patanaṃ tan mahad duḥkhaṃ paritāpaḥ sudāruṇaḥ svargabhājaś cyavantīha tasmāt svargaṃ na kāmaye
english: That great fall is misery, the anguish is truly terrible; those who partake of heaven fall back here — therefore I do not desire heaven.

sanskrit: yatra gatvā na śocanti na vyathanti calanti vā tad ahaṃ sthānam atyantaṃ mārgayiṣyāmi kevalam
english: That place where, having gone, one neither grieves nor trembles nor wavers — I shall seek that state alone, absolutely and without exception.

sanskrit: ity uktvā sa munir vākyaṃ devadūtaṃ visṛjya tam śiloñchavṛttim utsṛjya śamam ātiṣṭhad uttamam
english: Having spoken these words, that sage dismissed the divine messenger and, abandoning the gleaning-of-grain livelihood, he established himself in the highest tranquility.

sanskrit: tulyanindāstutir bhūtvā samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ jñānayogena śuddhena dhyānanityo babhūva ha
english: Becoming equal toward blame and praise, treating clods, stones, and gold alike, through pure union with knowledge he became perpetually absorbed in meditation.

sanskrit: dhyānayogād balaṃ labdhvā prāpya carddhim anuttamām jagāma śāśvatīṃ siddhiṃ parāṃ nirvāṇalakṣaṇām
english: Having gained strength through the yoga of meditation and attained the unsurpassable power, he reached eternal and supreme perfection, marked by nirvana.

sanskrit: tasmāt tvam api kaunteya na śokaṃ kartum arhasi rājyāt sphītāt paribhraṣṭas tapasā tad avāpsyasi
english: Therefore you too, O son of Kuntī, ought not to grieve; though fallen from a flourishing kingdom, you shall recover it through austerity.

sanskrit: sukhasyānantaraṃ duḥkhaṃ duḥkhasyānantaraṃ sukham paryāyeṇopavartante naraṃ nemim arā iva
english: After happiness comes sorrow, and after sorrow comes happiness; they revolve in turn upon a man as spokes upon a wheel's rim.

sanskrit: pitṛpaitāmahaṃ rājyaṃ prāpsyasy amitavikrama varṣāt trayodaśād ūrdhvaṃ vyetu te mānaso jvaraḥ
english: O one of immeasurable valor, you shall recover the ancestral kingdom after thirteen years are past — let the fever of grief depart from your mind.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā sa bhagavān vyāsaḥ pāṇḍavanandanam jagāma tapase dhīmān punar evāśramaṃ prati
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, that blessed Vyāsa, the wise one, left the son of the Pāṇḍavas and went back once more to his hermitage for austerity.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasmin bahumṛge 'raṇye ramamāṇā mahārathāḥ kāmyake bharataśreṣṭhā vijahrus te yathāmarāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: In that forest teeming with deer, the great warriors, the foremost among the Bhāratas, sported in the Kāmyaka forest like the immortals.

sanskrit: prekṣamāṇā bahuvidhān vanoddeśān samantataḥ yathartukālaramyāś ca vanarājīḥ supuṣpitāḥ
english: Surveying on all sides the many kinds of forest regions and the rows of trees beautifully flowering as befitted each season,

sanskrit: pāṇḍavā mṛgayāśīlāś carantas tan mahāvanam vijahrur indrapratimāḥ kaṃ cit kālam ariṃdamāḥ
english: the Pāṇḍavas, fond of the hunt, roaming through that great forest, sported for a time — those tamers of foes, peers of Indra.

sanskrit: tatas te yaugapadyena yayuḥ sarve caturdiśam mṛgayāṃ puruṣavyāghrā brāhmaṇārthe paraṃtapāḥ
english: Then all of them, those tigers among men, those scorchers of foes, went out simultaneously in the four directions for the hunt, for the sake of a brahmin.

sanskrit: draupadīm āśrame nyasya tṛṇabindor anujñayā maharṣer dīptatapaso dhaumyasya ca purodhasaḥ
english: Having left Draupadī in the hermitage, with the permission of the great seer Tṛṇabindu of blazing austerity and of the priest Dhaumya,

sanskrit: tatas tu rājā sindhūnāṃ vārddhakṣatrir mahāyaśāḥ vivāhakāmaḥ śālveyān prayātaḥ so 'bhavat tadā
english: at that time the king of the Sindhus, Vṛddhakṣatra's son, the greatly renowned one, was traveling toward the Shalveyas with desire for marriage.

sanskrit: mahatā paribarheṇa rājayogyena saṃvṛtaḥ rājabhir bahubhiḥ sārdham upāyāt kāmyakaṃ ca saḥ
english: Surrounded by great pomp fit for a king, along with many kings, he came to the Kāmyaka forest.

sanskrit: tatrāpaśyat priyāṃ bhāryāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ yaśasvinīm tiṣṭhantīm āśramadvāri draupadīṃ nirjane vane
english: There he saw the beloved and renowned wife of the Pāṇḍavas, Draupadī, standing at the hermitage gate in the lonely forest.

sanskrit: vibhrājamānāṃ vapuṣā bibhratīṃ rūpam uttamam bhrājayantīṃ vanoddeśaṃ nīlābhram iva vidyutam
english: Blazing with beauty, bearing a surpassing form, illuminating that forest region like lightning against a dark cloud —

sanskrit: apsarā devakanyā vā māyā vā devanirmitā iti kṛtvāñjaliṃ sarve dadṛśus tām aninditām
english: "An apsara, or a daughter of the gods, or an illusion fashioned by the gods?" — thinking thus, all of them, joining their palms, gazed at that blameless one.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā sindhūnāṃ vārddhakṣatrir jayadrathaḥ vismitas tām anindyāṅgīṃ dṛṣṭvāsīd dhṛṣṭamānasaḥ
english: Then that king of the Sindhus, Vṛddhakṣatra's son Jayadratha, was astonished upon seeing that woman of blameless limbs, and his mind grew bold with desire.

sanskrit: sa koṭikāśyaṃ rājānam abravīt kāmamohitaḥ kasya tv eṣānavadyāṅgī yadi vāpi na mānuṣī
english: Bewildered by desire, he spoke to King Kotikashya: "Whose is this woman of faultless limbs — or is she perhaps not even human?"

sanskrit: vivāhārtho na me kaś cid imāṃ dṛṣṭvātisundarīm etām evāham ādāya gamiṣyāmi svam ālayam
english: "Having seen this exceedingly beautiful one, I have no interest in any other for marriage — I shall take this very one and go to my own home."

sanskrit: gaccha jānīhi saumyaināṃ kasya kā ca kuto 'pi vā kimartham āgatā subhrūr idaṃ kaṇṭakitaṃ vanam
english: "Go and find out about her, O gentle one — whose wife is she, who is she, where does she come from, and why has this fair-browed lady come to this thorny forest?"

sanskrit: api nāma varārohā mām eṣā lokasundarī bhajed adyāyatāpāṅgī sudatī tanumadhyamā
english: "O may this woman of noble hips, a beauty of the world, with long sidelong eyes, fine teeth, and slender waist, choose me today."

sanskrit: apy ahaṃ kṛtakāmaḥ syām imāṃ prāpya varastriyam gaccha jānīhi ko nv asyā nātha ity eva koṭika
english: "Might I have my desire fulfilled by winning this noble woman? Go and find out who is her lord — thus, O Koṭika."

sanskrit: sa koṭikāśyas tac chrutvā rathāt praskandya kuṇḍalī upetya papraccha tadā kroṣṭā vyāghravadhūm iva
english: Kotikashya, hearing that, leapt down from his chariot, his earrings swaying, and approached her; then he questioned her as a jackal might question a tigress.

sanskrit: koṭikāśya uvāca kā tvaṃ kadambasya vinamya śākhām; ekāśrame tiṣṭhasi śobhamānā dedīpyamānāgniśikheva naktaṃ; dodhūyamānā pavanena subhrūḥ
english: Kotikashya said: Who are you who, bending a branch of the kadamba tree, stand radiant in this hermitage, blazing like a flame in the night, swaying in the breeze, O fair-browed one?

sanskrit: atīva rūpeṇa samanvitā tvaṃ; na cāpy araṇyeṣu bibheṣi kiṃ nu devī nu yakṣī yadi dānavī vā; varāpsarā daityavarāṅganā vā
english: You are endowed with surpassing beauty, and yet you have no fear in these forests — are you a goddess, a yakshi, a danaví, a foremost apsara, or the finest consort of the daityas?

sanskrit: vapuṣmatī voragarājakanyā; vanecarī vā kṣaṇadācarastrī yady eva rājño varuṇasya patnī; yamasya somasya dhaneśvarasya
english: A shapely serpent-king's daughter, a forest-dweller, a woman who walks by night, or perhaps the queen of King Varuṇa, of Yama, of Soma, or of Kubera the lord of wealth?

sanskrit: dhātur vidhātuḥ savitur vibhor vā; śakrasya vā tvaṃ sadanāt prapannā na hy eva naḥ pṛcchasi ye vayaṃ sma; na cāpi jānīma taveha nātham
english: Have you come forth from the abode of Dhata, Vidhātā, the Sun, the Lord, or Indra? For you do not ask us who we are, nor do we know your lord here.

sanskrit: vayaṃ hi mānaṃ tava vardhayantaḥ; pṛcchāma bhadre prabhavaṃ prabhuṃ ca ācakṣva bandhūṃś ca patiṃ kulaṃ ca; tattvena yac ceha karoṣi kāryam
english: We ask you, O fortunate one, in order to honor you — tell us truly your origin and your lord; reveal your kinsmen, your husband, your lineage, and whatever business brings you here.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu rājñaḥ surathasya putro; yaṃ koṭikāśyeti vidur manuṣyāḥ asau tu yas tiṣṭhati kāñcanāṅge; rathe huto 'gniś cayane yathaiva trigartarājaḥ kamalāyatākṣi; kṣemaṃkaro nāma sa eṣa vīraḥ
english: I am the son of King Suratha, known among men as Kotikashya. And he who stands in the golden-bodied chariot, like fire in an altar, is the Trigarta king — O lotus-eyed one, that hero is named Kshemankara.

sanskrit: asmāt paras tv eṣa mahādhanuṣmān; putraḥ kuṇindādhipater variṣṭhaḥ nirīkṣate tvāṃ vipulāyatāṃsaḥ; suvismitaḥ parvatavāsanityaḥ
english: Beyond him is this mighty archer, the foremost son of the lord of the Kuṇindas; he gazes at you with broad, long shoulders, greatly astonished — he is one who always dwells in the mountains.

sanskrit: asau tu yaḥ puṣkariṇīsamīpe; śyāmo yuvā tiṣṭhati darśanīyaḥ ikṣvākurājñaḥ subalasya putraḥ; sa eṣa hantā dviṣatāṃ sugātri
english: And that dark youth who stands near the lotus pool, so handsome to behold, is the son of the Ikṣvāku king Subala — he, O one of fair limbs, is the slayer of enemies.

sanskrit: yasyānuyātraṃ dhvajinaḥ prayānti; sauvīrakā dvādaśa rājaputrāḥ śoṇāśvayukteṣu ratheṣu sarve; makheṣu dīptā iva havyavāhāḥ
english: In whose retinue march twelve Sauvīra princes bearing banners, all in chariots yoked with reddish horses, blazing like sacrificial fires at a great rite —

sanskrit: aṅgārakaḥ kuñjaraguptakaś ca; śatruṃjayaḥ saṃjayasupravṛddhau prabhaṃkaro 'tha bhramaro raviś ca; śūraḥ pratāpaḥ kuharaś ca nāma
english: Angara, Kunjaraputaka, Shatrunjaya, Sañjaya and Supravriddha, Prabhankara, Bhamara, Ravi, Śūra, Pratapa, and Kuhara by name —

sanskrit: yaṃ ṣaṭsahasrā rathino 'nuyānti; nāgā hayāś caiva padātinaś ca jayadratho nāma yadi śrutas te; sauvīrarājaḥ subhage sa eṣaḥ
english: whom six thousand charioteers follow, along with elephants, horses, and foot soldiers — if you have heard of Jayadratha, O fortunate one, that is he, the king of the Sauvīras.

sanskrit: tasyāpare bhrātaro 'dīnasattvā; balāhakānīkavidāraṇādhyāḥ sauvīravīrāḥ pravarā yuvāno; rājānam ete balino 'nuyānti
english: His other brothers of undaunted spirit, experts in shattering armies of Balāhaka horses — foremost Sauvīra warriors, young and strong — these mighty ones follow the king.

sanskrit: etaiḥ sahāyair upayāti rājā; marudgaṇair indra ivābhiguptaḥ ajānatāṃ khyāpaya naḥ sukeśi; kasyāsi bhāryā duhitā ca kasya
english: The king advances with these companions, guarded like Indra by the hosts of Maruts — O beautiful-haired one, make yourself known to us who do not know: whose wife are you, and whose daughter?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca athābravīd draupadī rājaputrī; pṛṣṭā śibīnāṃ pravareṇa tena avekṣya mandaṃ pravimucya śākhāṃ; saṃgṛhṇatī kauśikam uttarīyam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the royal princess Draupadī, questioned by that foremost of the Śibis, slowly looked about, released the branch, and drawing up her silk upper garment, spoke.

sanskrit: buddhyābhijānāmi narendraputra; na mādṛśī tvām abhibhāṣṭum arhā na tveha vaktāsti taveha vākyam; anyo naro vāpy atha vāpi nārī
english: "I know you by intelligence, O son of a lord of men; a woman such as I is not fit to address you — and you have no words to say to me here, nor has any other man or woman."

sanskrit: ekā hy ahaṃ saṃprati tena vācaṃ; dadāni vai bhadra nibodha cedam ahaṃ hy araṇye katham ekam ekā; tvām ālapeyaṃ niratā svadharme
english: "For I am alone here, and I speak to you only briefly; mark this well, O gentle one — how could I who am devoted to my own dharma address you alone, here alone in the forest?"

sanskrit: jānāmi ca tvāṃ surathasya putraṃ; yaṃ koṭikāśyeti vidur manuṣyāḥ tasmād ahaṃ śaibya tathaiva tubhyam; ākhyāmi bandhūn prati tan nibodha
english: "I know you as the son of Suratha, whom men know as Kotikashya; therefore, O Śaibya, I shall likewise tell you about my kinsmen — hear this well."

sanskrit: apatyam asmi drupadasya rājñaḥ; kṛṣṇeti māṃ śaibya vidur manuṣyāḥ sāhaṃ vṛṇe pañca janān patitve; ye khāṇḍavaprasthagatāḥ śrutās te
english: "I am the offspring of King Drupada; men know me as Kṛṣṇa, O Śaibya. I have chosen five men as husbands — those who went to Khāṇḍavaprastha, of whom you have heard."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiro bhīmasenārjunau ca; mādryāś ca putrau puruṣapravīrau te māṃ niveśyeha diśaś catasro; vibhajya pārthā mṛgayāṃ prayātāḥ
english: "Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīmasena, Arjuna, and the two heroic sons of Mādrī — having settled me here, the Pārthas divided the four directions and have gone to the hunt."

sanskrit: prācīṃ rājā dakṣiṇāṃ bhīmaseno; jayaḥ pratīcīṃ yamajāv udīcīm manye tu teṣāṃ rathasattamānāṃ; kālo 'bhitaḥ prāpta ihopayātum
english: "The king went east, Bhīmasena south, Jaya west, the twin sons of Yama north — I believe the time for those finest of chariot-warriors to return here has all but arrived."

sanskrit: saṃmānitā yāsyatha tair yatheṣṭaṃ; vimucya vāhān avagāhayadhvam priyātithir dharmasuto mahātmā; prīto bhaviṣyaty abhivīkṣya yuṣmān
english: "Honored by them you shall depart as you wish; unharness your horses and let them drink — the great-souled son of Dharma, who loves guests, will be pleased to see you."

sanskrit: etāvad uktvā drupadātmajā sā; śaibyātmajaṃ candramukhī pratītā viveśa tāṃ parṇakuṭīṃ praśastāṃ; saṃcintya teṣām atithisvadharmam
english: Having said thus much, that moon-faced daughter of Drupada, the confident one, entered that excellent leaf-hut, reflecting on the dharma of hosting guests on their behalf.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca athāsīneṣu sarveṣu teṣu rājasu bhārata koṭikāśyavacaḥ śrutvā śaibyaṃ sauvīrako 'bravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, O Bhārata, when all those kings were seated and had heard Kotikashya's words, the Sauvīra king spoke to Śaibya.

sanskrit: yadā vācaṃ vyāharantyām asyāṃ me ramate manaḥ sīmantinīnāṃ mukhyāyāṃ vinivṛttaḥ kathaṃ bhavān
english: "When she was speaking, my mind delighted in this foremost among parted-hair women — how then can you turn back?"

sanskrit: etāṃ dṛṣṭvā striyo me 'nyā yathā śākhāmṛgastriyaḥ pratibhānti mahābāho satyam etad bravīmi te
english: "Having seen her, O mighty-armed one, other women appear to me like she-monkeys — I tell you this truly."

sanskrit: darśanād eva hi manas tayā me 'pahṛtaṃ bhṛśam tāṃ samācakṣva kalyāṇīṃ yadi syāc chaibya mānuṣī
english: "For by merely seeing her, my mind has been wholly stolen away by her; tell me about that auspicious one, O Śaibya — is she human?"

sanskrit: koṭikāśya uvāca eṣā vai draupadī kṛṣṇā rājaputrī yaśasvinī pañcānāṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ mahiṣī saṃmatā bhṛśam
english: Kotikashya said: "This is indeed Draupadī, the dark princess, the renowned one, held in the highest esteem as the queen consort of the five sons of Pāṇḍu."

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ caiva pārthānāṃ priyā bahumatā satī tayā sametya sauvīra suvīrān susukhī vraja
english: "Dear and highly esteemed by all the Pārthas, she is a woman of virtue — O Sauvīra, go meet with her, then proceed happily among great heroes."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktaḥ pratyuvāca paśyāmo draupadīm iti patiḥ sauvīrasindhūnāṃ duṣṭabhāvo jayadrathaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, Jayadratha, lord of the Sauvīras and Sindhus, wicked-hearted, replied: "We shall see Draupadī."

sanskrit: sa praviśyāśramaṃ śūnyaṃ siṃhagoṣṭhaṃ vṛko yathā ātmanā saptamaḥ kṛṣṇām idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: He entered the empty hermitage like a wolf entering a lion's lair, himself the seventh, and spoke these words to Kṛṣṇa (Draupadī).

sanskrit: kuśalaṃ te varārohe bhartāras te 'py anāmayāḥ yeṣāṃ kuśalakāmāsi te 'pi kaccid anāmayāḥ
english: "Are you well, O noble-hipped one? Are your husbands also free from ailment? Those for whose welfare you care — are they too free from illness?"

sanskrit: draupady uvāca kauravyaḥ kuśalī rājā kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ ahaṃ ca bhrātaraś cāsya yāṃś cānyān paripṛcchasi
english: Draupadī said: "The Kaurava king Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī, is well; I am well, his brothers are well — and those others you ask after too."

sanskrit: pādyaṃ pratigṛhāṇedam āsanaṃ ca nṛpātmaja mṛgān pañcāśataṃ caiva prātarāśaṃ dadāni te
english: "Accept this water for your feet, and a seat as well, O son of a king; and five hundred deer — I offer you a morning meal."

sanskrit: aiṇeyān pṛṣatān nyaṅkūn hariṇāñ śarabhāñ śaśān ṛśyān rurūñ śambarāṃś ca gavayāṃś ca mṛgān bahūn
english: "Black antelope, spotted deer, nyankus, hariṇas, sharabhas, hares, rishyas, rurus, shambaras, gavyas, and many other deer —"

sanskrit: varāhān mahiṣāṃś caiva yāś cānyā mṛgajātayaḥ pradāsyati svayaṃ tubhyaṃ kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: "— boars and buffalo, and whatever other kinds of game there are — Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī, will himself give to you."

sanskrit: jayadratha uvāca kuśalaṃ prātarāśasya sarvā me 'pacitiḥ kṛtā ehi me ratham āroha sukham āpnuhi kevalam
english: Jayadratha said: "Enough of a morning meal — all due honor has been rendered to me; come, mount my chariot, and enjoy happiness alone."

sanskrit: gataśrīkāṃś cyutān rājyāt kṛpaṇān gatacetasaḥ araṇyavāsinaḥ pārthān nānuroddhuṃ tvam arhasi
english: "The Pārthas have lost their glory, fallen from their kingdom, pitiable, broken in spirit, dwelling in the forest — you ought not to bind yourself to them."

sanskrit: na vai prājñā gataśrīkaṃ bhartāram upayuñjate yuñjānam anuyuñjīta na śriyaḥ saṃkṣaye vaset
english: "Wise women do not attach themselves to a husband bereft of fortune; one should attach oneself to a husband who is active and prospering — one should not dwell where prosperity has dried up."

sanskrit: śriyā vihīnā rājyāc ca vinaṣṭāḥ śāśvatīḥ samāḥ alaṃ te pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ bhaktyā kleśam upāsitum
english: "Deprived of fortune and of their kingdom, destroyed for years without end — enough of this trouble of devotion to the sons of Pāṇḍu."
